newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Canadian stocks set to consolidate.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Canadian stocks set to consolidate.

text.p: Consolidation is expected to temper the recent buoyancy of the Toronto stock exchange, according to the average of predictions for Canadian stocks in a Reuters survey on Wednesday.
Six analysts who took part in the poll made an average forecast for the TSE 300 index of just over 6,500 for the end of 1997, slightly better than the average prediction made three months ago.
The end-1997 forecast would be an improvement of nearly four percent on the closing level of 6,257.21 on March 12, the date of the survey.
At least one of the analysts had a more bearish outlook, saying he thought the market had already peaked for the year and was now set to decline.
RON MEISELS, PORTFOLIO CONSULTANT AND PRESIDENT, P AND C HOLDINGS:

"The market will be good for 1997. We may get a high sometime in July of maybe 6800, but then we'll get a back-off in the third and fourth quarters and into 1998. Next year we should end on a very strong note."
JOE ISMAIL, TECHNICAL ANALYST, MAISON PLACEMENTS CANADA:

"I'm looking for about a 10 percent pullback at least (by the end of 1997). I'm satisfied the market's just about peaked for the year. There will be profit-taking in the financial services sector and I see a pullback in oils, gold and metals."
MICHAEL METZ, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST, OPPENHEIMER AND CO:
"I'm looking for a boom in the whole industrial commodities sector."
